Friedrich Nietzsche, Thus Spake Zarathustra, translated by Thomas Common.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/friedrich-nietzsche/thus-spake-zarathustra/thomas-common

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Friedrich Nietzsche, the author, died 1900.
- Thomas Common, the translator, died 1919.

First publication of the text used: 1909 (SE colophon: 'Thus Spake Zarathustra was published between 1883 and 1885 by Friedrich Nietzsche. It was translated from German in 1909 by Thomas Common.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the Standard Ebooks rights statement says the text is in the US public domain, and the text was a translation first published in 1909, before 1931, so it is public domain there.
- Country of origin: every person named above died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die did so in 1919, so this holds by 1 January 2020.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
